passage: Looking back, I can still see it. Irawati was standing at the front of the class while three boys imitated her walk, and half the room was laughing. I laughed too, just once, a small breath through my nose, before I felt sick. Nobody said a word. I stayed in my seat and pretended to look for my pencil. All day I kept replaying it, ashamed that I'd done nothing, ashamed that I'd laughed. That evening I decided it mattered even if it was small. I sent Irawati a note in her locker: "That was not okay. I'm sorry I laughed. I'm here if you want to talk." The next day I told the class teacher what happened. Since then, when I hear that kind of joke, I don't laugh. I'm Sarika, and it isn't much, but it's mine to do.

qa.q: Where was Irawati standing when the boys imitated her walk?
qa.a: She was standing at the front of the class.

qa.q: What was Sarika feeling after the incident?
qa.a: Ashamed. Sarika kept replaying it and felt bad both about doing nothing and about laughing once.

qa.q: What small steps did Sarika take?
qa.a: Sarika left a kind note in Irawati's locker, told the class teacher the next day and decided not to laugh at that kind of joke again.

qa.q: How might Irawati have felt reading Sarika's note?
qa.a: Probably relieved and less alone, because someone who had been in the room said it was not okay.

grounding: Sarika saw a classmate bullied, did nothing and felt ashamed, then checked on her privately, reported to a teacher and refused to laugh.

passage:
Class teacher's note, Class 8C, Friday
Zainab stayed back after the last period, looking at the floor. She said that on Wednesday, in the lunch queue, some boys had knocked Sumit's tray and poured water on his notebook while others filmed. She stood there and did nothing. Some people laughed. She said she didn't, "but I didn't stop it either."
She was clearly ashamed. I told her that telling me now was a real and important step, and that small acts matter.
She named the boys and said the video was in a group chat. I noted the details and told the principal before she left. I also asked her whether she'd feel able to sit with Sumit at lunch next week. She said she'd already messaged him that evening to say sorry.
I spoke to Sumit's parents by phone at 4 p.m. The boys and their parents will meet the principal on Monday.

qa.q: What did the boys pour water on?
How did Zainab feel when she came to the teacher?
qa.a: She felt ashamed and guilty, looking at the floor because she had watched and done nothing.

qa.q: What small acts did Zainab take, and why do they matter?
qa.a: She reported the incident, named the boys and messaged Sumit to say sorry, which brought adult action and showed Sumit someone cared.

qa.q: What was the lunch queue like for Sumit?
qa.a: Sumit likely felt humiliated and helpless, with his tray knocked, his notebook soaked and people filming and laughing.

grounding: A teen who watched a classmate being bullied and did nothing feels ashamed, then reports it and checks on him.

passage:
Thursday
I watched it happen again today. In the changing room after PE, Riddhi and her friends hid Tenzin's uniform and laughed while she searched, and then said her Hindi sounded "funny." Everyone laughed. I didn't laugh, but I didn't say anything. I just tied my shoes very slowly.
I felt disgusting all afternoon. It's been going on for weeks.
So after the last bell I found Tenzin at the bus stop. I said, "I'm sorry about today. That wasn't okay." She looked surprised and said, "No one's said that before."
Then I went back inside to Ms D'Souza's room. I told her everything I'd seen, the uniform, the names, the dates I could remember. She wrote it down and said, "Thank you, Mahima. This took courage." She called Tenzin's mother before I left.
Tomorrow I'm going to sit with Tenzin at lunch. And if they start again, I won't laugh or look away.

qa.q: Where did Riddhi and her friends hide Tenzin's uniform?
qa.a: In the changing room after PE.

qa.q: How did Mahima feel after watching and saying nothing?
qa.a: Mahima felt disgusting and ashamed all afternoon, knowing it had been going on for weeks.

qa.q: Which small acts did Mahima choose, and why do they matter?
qa.a: Mahima checked on Tenzin privately, reported it to Ms D'Souza the same day and plans to sit with her, which brings help and breaks Tenzin's isolation.

qa.q: How does Tenzin react when Mahima says sorry?
qa.a: Tenzin is surprised and moved, since no one had ever said that to her before.

grounding: A teen who watched a classmate being bullied feels ashamed, checks on her privately and reports it to a teacher.
